summary: SEBI, India's securities regulator, is requiring the top 500 companies listed on stock exchanges to spend at least 10% of their Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) budgets on instruments issued by non-profit organizations (NPOs) on the new Social Stock Exchange (SSE). This is part of an effort to make social welfare funding more accessible and support the new SSE platform.
impact: This means your company will need to adjust its CSR spending strategy. A portion of the CSR budget must now be directed towards purchasing specific financial instruments (like bonds) from NPOs listed on the SSE. This requires coordination with your CSR team and ensuring compliance with the new spending requirement.
benefits: This regulation encourages companies to actively contribute to social causes by directing funds specifically to NPOs through a transparent platform. It helps maximize the impact of CSR spending and supports the development of a dedicated infrastructure for social impact investing.
flash_alerts: Allocate at least 10% of your company's annual CSR budget specifically for purchases on the Social Stock Exchange (SSE).
Coordinate closely with your Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) team to ensure compliance with this new spending requirement.
